chunks: The khums (one-fifth) is obligatory in everything that reaches a dinar in value, from treasures, minerals, diving, and war spoils. It belongs to Allah — the Mighty and Majestic — His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), the near kin from the wealthy and the poor, the orphans, the needy, and the traveler among the people of the religion.
Fasting for the year consists of three days in each month: a Thursday at its beginning, a Wednesday in its middle, and a Thursday at its end.

Fasting the month of Ramadan is an obligation and is determined by moon-sighting, not by opinion or conjecture. Whoever fasts before the sighting or breaks his fast before the sighting has opposed the religion of the Imamiyya. The testimony of women is not accepted in divorce, nor in the sighting of the crescent.

Prayer in the month of Ramadan is the same as prayer in other months. Whoever wishes to add more should pray twenty rak'ahs each night: eight rak'ahs between Maghrib and the final Isha, and twelve rak'ahs after the final Isha, until twenty nights of Ramadan have passed. Then he prays thirty rak'ahs each night: eight between Maghrib and Isha, and twenty-two after Isha. In each rak'ah one recites al-Fatiha and whatever is easy of the Quran — except on the night of the twenty-first and the night of the twenty-third, for it is recommended to keep vigil in both, and that one prays one hundred rak'ahs each of those nights, reciting al-Fatiha once and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad ten times in each rak'ah. Whoever spends these two nights reviewing knowledge — that is better.

key_terms.إِحْيَاء: Ihya' — to 'give life' to a night by filling it with worship; keeping vigil on a sacred night.
key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةُ: Ru'ya — the physical sighting of the crescent moon used to determine the beginning and end of Ramadan, as opposed to calculation or conjecture.
key_terms.الْإِمَامِيَّةُ: Imamiyya — the Twelver Shia school, used here as a self-identifying term to define orthodox practice.
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: Khums — the one-fifth religious tax obligatory on specific categories of earnings and wealth, distributed to designated recipients including the Imam's share and descendants of the Prophet.
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ النِّسَاءِ: Testimony of women — the tradition rules that women's testimony is inadmissible in divorce proceedings and moon-sighting determinations.
key_terms.مُذَاكَرَةُ الْعِلْمِ: Mudhakarat al-'ilm — mutual review, discussion, and study of religious knowledge, presented as superior to additional prayers on Laylat al-Qadr.

ai.seo_question: What are the Imami rulings on khums, Ramadan fasting, and the special prayers on Laylat al-Qadr according to al-Saduq's Amali?
ai.summary: This tradition, recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq's Amali (the 93rd assembly, dated Sha'ban 368 AH), transmits a concise compendium of Imami jurisprudential rulings covering three topics: the distribution and categories of khums (the one-fifth alms-tax), the recommended fasting days and rules governing Ramadan (including the requirement for moon-sighting and inadmissibility of women's testimony in crescent sighting), and the voluntary additional prayers in Ramadan with specific schedules for different nights. The text explicitly identifies violators of the moon-sighting rule as opponents of 'the religion of the Imamiyya,' signaling a polemical stance against those who use calculation or opinion to determine Ramadan. The closing remark that reviewing religious knowledge on the two holy nights (the 21st and 23rd of Ramadan, associated with Laylat al-Qadr in Shia tradition) is superior to additional rak'ahs reflects the tradition's high valuation of 'ilm.
